headline: Every roll checked before it is wrapped and shipped.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: GALE Pacific has made technical fabrics for 75 years and made the world's first knitted shade fabric in the 1970s. Once fabric is rolled, wrapped and labelled, the label is all your customer has to go on. This is what a camera check could look like at the end of a roll finishing line, as an example. The same kind of camera can also watch the fabric itself as it runs, for holes, snags and colour changes. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every roll is wrapped and taped, with no loose ends or torn wrap. A roll that unwinds or gets dirty in transit is a claim from the customer.
labelLede: Charcoal and olive shade fabric can look much the same under the wrap. The camera checks every roll carries the right label for the colour, width and length inside, straight and complete.
codeLede: Batch and roll numbers tie every roll back to its production run. The system reads the ticket on every roll and compares it with the batch set at changeover.
objectLede: Core offcuts, tape and loose packaging can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the line spots anything that should not be there before rolls are palletised.
